population: Finnish men: 43 long-lived healthy men and 63 healthy men of mean age 83, against 92 men who had died of natural causes at mean age 66.6
conclusion: Direct sequencing of the SIRT6 exons found the T allele more often in the men who had died at a mean age of 66.6 than in the two long-lived healthy groups combined, giving an odds ratio of 3.58 against the T allele for longevity. At p = 0.074 this does not reach the study's own stated 0.05 threshold, and the authors report a statistical power of 28.4 per cent and state that 427 cases and 371 controls would be needed to reach 80 per cent, so this is a trend rather than a finding. Two transcription notes for anyone re-reading the source: the abstract states this odds ratio as 3.53 while the Results text and Table 2 both give 3.58, and the value recorded here is the table's; and this paper describes rs117385980 as an intron variant 23 bases downstream of the exon 2 exon/intron border.
study_design: Case-control, two-tailed Fisher exact test on two combined Finnish cohorts (n = 198), Sanger sequencing of SIRT6 exons and flanking regions
provenance_quote: These study findings suggest an inverse association between the T allele of rs117385980 and longevity in Finnish men.

population: Iranian adults aged 60 to 90 from the Birjand Longitudinal Aging Study (n = 227), stratified by Fried frailty phenotype and by age band
conclusion: The paper's primary question, whether the T allele associates with frailty, returned nothing: the allele was absent from the frail group and present at 2.13 per cent in the non-frail group, p = 0.36, and every adjusted regression model crossed one. The longevity-relevant result is secondary: an allele-frequency trend across three age bands at p = 0.073, with the T allele absent from all 40 participants aged 80 to 90 and present at 1.39 and 4.65 per cent in the two younger bands. No effect size is recorded beside that p-value because the three-band trend test does not produce one; a pairwise 70-79 against 80-90 comparison in the same paper gave p = 0.06, which is a different test and is not paired here. The same allele was slightly more common among robust than among frail participants, which points the opposite way, and the authors describe the effect as diverse. Note also that this paper calls rs117385980 a stop-gained variant in exon 2, which conflicts with the intron-variant description in the Finnish study it sets out to replicate.
study_design: Exploratory case-control within a population cohort, PCR-RFLP genotyping with Sanger confirmation on three samples, chi-square and Fisher exact tests plus adjusted logistic regression
provenance_quote: Although our findings did not reveal a significant association, a potential inverse association was observed between T allele of rs117385980 variant and individuals aged 80 years and over.
